_doc: Large batch L01 themed pass (TEMPLATE.md sections 9 and 10): dingo, foxes, bramble wolves, wolverine, badgers. New motifs live in motifs/large_L01.js; every piece (unique and class) has a hand note. All 10 signature motifs are new; 8 of them are used by no other creature (mousing-arc and briar-vine are lent to sibling foxes / the elder wolf).

alpha-dingo.notes: Alpha dingo of the desert: sandy ginger with a thick neck ruff and a torn, scarred ear; leads the pack, howls the signal, picks up burrs in its coat.

u0.n: Alpha Bite: the ruffed alpha head slams out, jaws wide, and snaps shut in a puff of sand

u1.n: Pack Signal: dingo muzzles go up at spots round the edge, tied by signal lines, howl arcs answering each other

u2.n: Burr Coat: spiky desert burrs caught in the ruff bristle out and cling

u3.n: Flank Run: two lean dingoes peel off and run wide round the flank, sand puffing at each stride

b0.n: Dingo Scrabble: dingoes scrabble out and back, paw prints scratched in the sand

b1.n: Dingo Pack Rush: the whole pack streams along the edge in one file

b2.n: Dingo Stand: ruffed heads stand in a row along the edge, jaws half open, growling

b3.n: Dingo Howl: a muzzle is thrown up and the howl arcs slam out over the sand

x0.n: Dingo Pounce: the alpha's head leaps off the edge on a dotted arc, jaws open

red-fox.notes: Red fox: russet coat and a huge white-tipped brush; sly, quick, a mousing hop; the tail is the thing you see as it slips away.

u0.n: Sly Pounce: the fox arcs up and dives nose-first at a different spot each time, never where you look

u1.n: Quick Bite: small sharp jaws dart off the edge and snap, click marks flashing

u2.n: Den Dash: little earths pop out round the edge, a face ducking into each, soil flicked up

u3.n: Brush Feint: the white-tipped brush swishes out and back; the tail is all you get

b0.n: Dragon-Smile Rake: a wide toothy fox grin rakes off the edge

b1.n: Rusty Scruff Lunge: the rusty fox lunges the length of the edge in one long leap

b2.n: Russet Ruff: russet brushes curl along the edge like a ruff and hold

b3.n: Sidle Past: a slim red fox trots out sideways and slips back

x0.n: Vixen Body-Check: the vixen leaps and lands shoulder-first, a dust puff where she hits

silver-fox.notes: Silver fox of the mountains: black fur with every hair tipped silver, thin pale legs; wary, slinking low, and it takes its tithe.

u0.n: Silver Pounce: silver-tipped guard hairs flare and strike off the edge, glinting

u1.n: Drift Dive: the dark fox dives into the drift at spot after spot, tied by its own track, snow flying

u2.n: Frost Pelt Fold: the black pelt folds along the edge and the silver tips frost over

u3.n: Pelt Tax: silver coins flip up off the edge: the fox collects its tax

b0.n: Silver Tip Swipe: a silver-tipped swipe runs the edge, the tips flashing in turn

b1.n: Tithe Bite: thin dark jaws snap, a silver glint at the fang

b2.n: Silver Wary Crouch: the tufts flatten and slip out and back, wary

b3.n: Sly Sidestep: the slim fox hops sideways from spot to spot

x0.n: Snowdrop Pounce: the fox arcs high and drops into the snow, a white puff

arctic-fox.notes: Arctic fox in its white winter coat: curls into a ball in the snow with its tail over its nose, vanishes in a whiteout, dives head-first into drifts.

u0.n: Snow Dive: a white fox arcs and dives head-first into the drift, snow bursting up

u1.n: White Out: curled white foxes scatter into the snow and come back, lost in the white

u2.n: Cold Nip: small white jaws nip off the edge, snow flicking

u3.n: Snow Veil: a veil of snowflakes drifts down along the edge over the hidden fox

b0.n: Snowdrift Scratch: white paw prints scratch out of the drift

b1.n: Blizzard Mangle: jaws gnash out and back in a whirl of snow

b2.n: Snow-White Hunch: the fox hunches into a white ball along the edge, tail over its nose

b3.n: Whiteout Vanish: the white ball blinks out and turns up somewhere else in the snow

x0.n: Snowblind Slam: the fox leaps and slams down in a burst of snow

tundra-fox.notes: Tundra fox in its thin brown summer coat, no snow: lean and quick, mousing for lemmings in the thawing tussocks, coat full of seed burrs.

u0.n: Mouse Pounce: a thin brown fox arcs high and slams nose-first into the tussock, soil flying

u1.n: Den Shove: the den mouth heaves out and back, earth shoved off the edge

u2.n: Thick Summer Coat: the brown coat bristles with caught burrs and seed heads

u3.n: Thaw Bite: jaws snap and drop away, meltwater beads running along the edge

b0.n: Thaw-Grudge Rake: brown paw prints rake off the edge in the thawing mud

b1.n: Tawny Pounce: a tawny fox leaps the length of the edge

b2.n: Lean-Brown Guard: thin brown foxes crouch low along the edge, ready to spring

b3.n: Unforgiving Shove: the lean fox shoulders out and back, kicking up soil

x0.n: Pounce-After Slam: a second pounce off the edge, a puff where it lands

bramble-wolf.notes: Bramble wolf of the forest: a grey-green wolf grown through with bramble canes, red-tipped hooked thorns in its fur; it hunts in a pack and howls.

u0.n: Howl: grey-green muzzles rise at spot after spot, howl arcs rolling out

u1.n: Bramble Bite: thorny jaws slam out and clamp, briar snapping

u2.n: Pack Circle: the pack circles and hooked briar canes bristle all round the edge

u3.n: Soil Scent: wolves cast out nose-down along the scent and come back, prints behind

b0.n: Briar Hook Swipe: hooked briar thorns swipe off the edge

b1.n: Thorn-Wrap Maul: canes wrap round and slam out with the maul

b2.n: Vine-Woven Bristle: woven canes line the edge, leaves opening, berries ripening

b3.n: Scent-Trail Dodge: a wolf blinks from spot to spot along its own scent trail

x0.n: Thicket Slam: a wolf bursts out of the thicket and back

elder-bramble-wolf.notes: Elder bramble wolf: grey muzzle, scarred, wearing a thick living ruff of green thorns that drains strength from what it catches; old, slow, wily.

u0.n: Thorn Lunge: thorny canes catch at spots along the edge, tied together, pulling tight

u1.n: Bramble Snap: grey-muzzled jaws snap out quick, an old wolf's bite

u2.n: Hedge Dodge: the thorn-ruffed elder ducks into the hedge and out again

u3.n: Ruff Shake: the thick thorn ruff shakes and bristles out, old leaves falling

b0.n: Bramble Ruff Swipe: the ruffed face swipes off the edge, thorns first

b1.n: Grey Beard Maul: old grey jaws maul out and back

b2.n: Living Ruff: the living ruff greens along the edge, sap beads running back to it

b3.n: Veteran Shoulder: the old wolf shoulders out and back

x0.n: Wily Pounce: the old wolf leaps out wily and low

wolverine.notes: Grumpy wolverine of the tundra: a squat dark-brown face with a pale headband, permanently cross, shaggy coat with a pale side band; never backs down.

u0.n: Grump Snarl: scowling faces pop up at spot after spot, snarling, grumble scribbles over them

u1.n: Ripping Bite: heavy jaws rip down the edge in one line

u2.n: Thick Fur: shaggy fur locks hang along the edge, the pale band swaying

u3.n: Cornered Rage: the furious face slams out, angry marks popping

b0.n: Snarling Rake: a snarling face lunges off the edge

b1.n: Grudge Gnash: jaws gnash out and back, grinding

b2.n: Stubborn Hunker: the shaggy coat flattens along the edge and will not move, snow settling on it

b3.n: Tantrum Shove: grumpy faces stamp out and back, kicking up dirt

x0.n: Sulky Pounce: a squat dark shape lollops off the edge

badger.notes: Badger: grizzled grey back, black-and-white striped face, huge spade claws; digs in, lives in a sett, bashes back.

u0.n: Dig In: earth arches rise along the edge, a striped face peering out of each hole

u1.n: Badger Maul: spade claws rake off the edge, soil flung

u2.n: Bash Back: the badger digs in and bashes back, claws out, dust flying

u3.n: Tunnel Dash: holes pop open round the edge and the badger dashes from one to the next

b0.n: Spade-Claw Dig: the claws dig a furrow along the edge, soil flung up

b1.n: Armoured Snout Ram: a striped snout rams out of the hole and back

b2.n: Striped Plate: the grizzled grey coat lies along the edge like a plate

b3.n: Burrow Dive: the badger dives into one hole and pops out of another

x0.n: Warren Bulldoze: the claws bulldoze off the edge in a cloud of dust

old-brock.notes: Old Brock: a wide old badger with a grey-white face and a scarred snout, tough-hided; keeps the old sett and charges toll on the path.

u0.n: Grey Maul: the wide grey-white face ploughs down the edge in one line, the scar showing

u1.n: Brock's Snap: old jaws snap off the edge, slow but sure

u2.n: Sett Wall: the old sett's earth arches push up like a wall, soil spraying

u3.n: Sett Tunnel: the sett's mouths line the edge, the old face looking out of each

b0.n: Digger's Rake: big clawed prints rake off the edge, soil thrown

b1.n: Path Toll Maul: brass toll coins are flung off the edge: pay to pass

b2.n: Silvered Hide: the silvered, tough old hide hangs thick along the edge

b3.n: Tunnel Shove: a tunnel mouth shoves out and back

x0.n: Grizzled Slam: the grizzled old face slams out, dust thumping up
